name: Acquired Amyloid Peripheral Neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Acquired Amyloid Peripheral Neuropathy Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of progressive sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy with distal symmetric distribution
Histopathological confirmation of amyloid deposits in nerve or tissue biopsy
Exclusion of hereditary amyloidosis by genetic testing
Evidence of cardiac amyloidosis on imaging or biomarkers
Presence of monoclonal gammopathy or abnormal serum free light chains

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Progressive sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy plus histopathological confirmation of amyloid deposits and exclusion of hereditary amyloidosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, pathological, and laboratory data to differentiate from hereditary forms.

searchTerms: nerve damage in hands and feet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Amyloid deposits confirmed by nerve biopsy

common.symptomName: Orthostatic hypotension due to autonomic neuropathy
searchTerms: dizziness on standing from nerve damage
weak muscles in hands and feet
loss of strength in distal limbs
muscle weakness in arms and legs

common.symptomName: Gastrointestinal dysmotility including diarrhea or constipation

occasional.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias related to amyloid infiltration
searchTerms: heart rhythm problems due to deposits

occasional.symptomName: Weight loss due to malabsorption or autonomic dysfunction
searchTerms: losing weight due to digestion issues
difficulty with erections from nerve issues
too little or too much sweating

rare.symptomName: Carpal tunnel syndrome secondary to amyloid deposition
searchTerms: carpal tunnel caused by protein deposits
hand numbness due to amyloid buildup

laboratory: Detection of monoclonal light chains in serum or urine
Elevated serum free light chain ratio
Abnormal nerve conduction studies showing axonal sensorimotor neuropathy
imaging: Cardiac MRI showing late gadolinium enhancement consistent with amyloid infiltration
genetic: Negative genetic testing for hereditary transthyretin or other amyloidosis mutations
other: Positive Congo red staining with apple-green birefringence under polarized light in biopsy samples

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of pathogenic mutations in amyloidogenic genes
Demyelinating features on nerve conduction studies
Absence of amyloid deposits on biopsy

redFlags: Rapidly progressive sensorimotor neuropathy with autonomic failure
Histological evidence of amyloid deposits in nerve or tissue biopsy
Presence of monoclonal gammopathy or abnormal serum free light chains
references: Gertz MA. Amyloidosis: diagnosis and treatment. Clin J Am Soc Nephrol. 2020.
Adams D, et al. Hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis: a model of medical progress for a fatal disease. Nat Rev Neurol. 2019.
Orphanet: Acquired amyloid peripheral neuropathy. ORPHA:209013.
